Our 2025 Senior Notes are senior unsecured obligations and may be redeemed at our option at any time at 100 % of the principal amount plus accrued interest and, until a specified period before maturity, a specified make-whole amount. Our 2025 Senior Notes contain a change-of-control provision that, under certain circumstances, may require us to purchase our 2025 Senior Notes at a price equal to 101 % of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest to the date of repurchase. We incurred approximately $ 13.9 million of costs associated with this offering which have been recorded as a reduction to the carrying amount of the debt on our consolidated balance sheets. These costs will be amortized as additional interest expense using the effective interest rate method over the period from issuance through maturity. The discounts will be amortized as additional interest expense over the period from issuance through maturity using the effective interest rate method. Interest on our 2031 Senior Notes is payable January 15 and July 15 of each year, commencing January 15, 2026. Interest on our 2035 Senior Notes and 2055 Senior Notes is payable May 15 and November 15 of each year, commencing on November 15, 2025. 2023 Term Loan Credit Agreement In connection with our acquisition of Reata in September 2023 we entered into a $ 1.5 billion term loan credit agreement. On the closing date of the Reata acquisition we drew $ 1.0 billion from the 2023 Term Loan, comprised of a $ 500.0 million floating rate 364-day tranche and a $ 500.0 million floating rate three-year tranche. The remaining unused commitment of $ 500.0 million was terminated. As of December 31, 2023, we repaid $ 350.0 million of the 364-day tranche. The remaining $ 150.0 million portion of the 364-day tranche was repaid during the first quarter of 2024.

passages.text: located in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY INTRODUCTION Biogen is a global biopharmaceutical company focused on discovering, developing and delivering innovative therapies for people living with serious and complex diseases. We have a broad portfolio of medicines to treat MS, have introduced the first approved treatment for SMA, co-developed treatments to address a defining pathology of Alzheimer’s disease and launched the first approved treatment to target a genetic cause of ALS. We market the first and only drug approved in the U.S., the E.U. and certain international markets for the treatment of FA in adults and adolescents aged 16 years and older. We are focused on advancing our pipeline in neurology, specialized immunology and rare diseases. We support our drug discovery and development efforts through internal research and development programs, external collaborations and acquisitions. Our marketed products include VUMERITY, TYSABRI, TECFIDERA, AVONEX and PLEGRIDY for the treatment of MS; SPINRAZA for the treatment of SMA; SKYCLARYS for the treatment of FA; and QALSODY for the treatment of ALS. We also have collaborations with Eisai on the commercialization of LEQEMBI for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease and Supernus on the commercialization of ZURZUVAE for the treatment of PPD. We have certain business and financial rights with respect to RITUXAN for the treatment of non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, CLL and other conditions; RITUXAN HYCELA for the treatment of non-Hodgkin's lymphoma and CLL; GAZYVA for the treatment of CLL, follicular lymphoma and, following its approval in October 2025, lupus nephritis; OCREVUS for the treatment of PPMS and RMS; LUNSUMIO for the treatment of relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma; COLUMVI, a bispecific antibody for the treatment of non-Hodgkin's lymphoma; and have the option to add other potential anti-CD20 therapies, pursuant to our collaboration arrangements with Genentech, a wholly owned member of the Roche Group. We commercialize a portfolio of biosimilars of advanced biologics including: BENEPALI, an etanercept biosimilar referencing ENBREL; IMRALDI, an adalimumab biosimilar referencing HUMIRA; and FLIXABI, an infliximab biosimilar referencing REMICADE. For additional information on our collaboration arrangements, please read Note 19, Collaborative and Other Relationships , to our consolidated financial statements included in this report. We seek to ensure an uninterrupted supply of medicines to patients around the world. To that end, we regularly review our manufacturing capacity, capabilities, processes and facilities. In order to support our future growth and drug development pipeline, we expanded our large molecule production capacity and built a large-scale biologics manufacturing facility in Solothurn, Switzerland. The Solothurn facility is operational and has been approved for the manufacture of LEQEMBI and TYSABRI. We believe that the Solothurn facility will support our anticipated near to mid-term needs for the manufacturing of biologic assets. The plant represents a significant increase in our overall manufacturing capacity. Additio

Our working capital was $5.6 billion as of December 31, 2025, compared to $1.9 billion as of December 31, 2024. The change in working capital reflects an increase in total current assets of approximately $1.5 billion and a decrease in total current liabilities of approximately $2.2 billion. The changes in total current assets and total current liabilities were primarily driven by the following: CURRENT ASSETS • $1.4 billion increase in cash, cash equivalents and current marketable securities ; • $62.4 million decrease in accounts receivable, net related to our ongoing operations; and • $292.4 million decrease in inventory primarily due to timing of production. CURRENT LIABILITIES • $1.7 billion decrease in the current portion of notes payable due to the redemption of our 4.050% Senior Notes due September 15, 2025, during the second quarter of 2025; and • $433.5 million decrease in taxes payable primarily due to the timing of tax payments. For additional information on our Senior Notes, please read Note 13, Indebtedness , to our consolidated financial statements included in this report. CASH, CASH EQUIVALENTS AND MARKETABLE SECURITIES As of December 31, 2025, we had cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaling approximately $4.2 billion compared to approximately $2.4 billion as of December 31, 2024. The increase in the balance was primarily due to cash generated by our operations, which includes $200.0 million of research and development funding received from Royalty Pharma, partially offset by worldwide tax payments of approximately $864.0 million, an upfront payment made to Stoke of $165.0 million in connection with the closing of our collaboration and license agreement, milestone payments made to the former shareholders of HI-Bio totaling $300.0 million, a payment of $50.0 million in connection with our acquisition of Alcyone and total payments of $166.0 million in connection with our agreements with City Therapeutics, Dayra and Vanqua. During the second quarter of 2025 we received $1.75 billion in net proceeds from the issuance of our 2025 Senior Notes, which was offset by a $1.75 billion payment made for the redemption of our 4.050% Senior Notes due September 15, 2025. Until required for another use in our business, we typically invest our cash reserves in bank deposits, certificates of deposit, commercial paper, corporate notes, U.S. and foreign government instruments, overnight reverse repurchase agreements and other interest-bearing marketable debt instruments in accordance with our investment policy. It is our policy to mitigate credit risk in our cash reserves and marketable securities by maintaining a well-diversified portfolio that limits the amount of exposure as to institution, maturity and investment type. We have experienced no significant limitations in our liquidity resulting from uncertainties in the banking sector. credit_strengths.text: Biogen's minimal leverage, with net debt to EBITDA net of cash and short-term investments below one time, sits well inside the sector median and reflects a conservatively financed balance sheet. The company's debt load has remained stable over the past three years, while cash generation has been sufficient to cover obligations.

Operating cash flow comfortably covers capital expenditures, producing free cash flow that represents a substantial portion of debt. This cash generation, combined with a current ratio above two and a half times, provides a strong liquidity cushion and supports the company's ability to meet near-term obligations without strain.

key_risks.text: The debt maturity profile is heavily weighted to later years, with no maturities in the next four years and a significant balloon in year five. While this reduces near-term refinancing risk, the company will need to address this concentration, potentially requiring refinancing in less favorable market conditions.

Revenue concentration in a limited number of marketed products and reliance on collaborations for key pipeline assets, such as LEQEMBI and ZURZUVAE, expose the company to competitive and regulatory risks. Additionally, the debt note discloses change-of-control provisions that could require repurchase at a premium, adding event risk.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage remains robust, with operating income covering interest expense multiple times over. This strong coverage, coupled with a substantial cash balance, provides ample capacity to service debt even if operating income were to decline significantly from current levels.

Free cash flow to debt is solid, and the company's cash flow generation has been consistent. However, the absence of disclosed dividend and buyback data limits visibility on shareholder distributions, which could absorb cash flow and reduce debt-servicing flexibility if pursued aggressively.

overall_credit_view.text: Biogen presents a strong credit profile, characterized by minimal leverage, robust interest coverage, and substantial liquidity. The company's operating performance has been stable, and its debt structure is manageable with no near-term maturities. The indicative financial risk profile is minimal, and the company is well positioned relative to sector peers.

Looking forward, the credit view is supported by expected continued cash generation and a manageable debt maturity profile. However, the company's exposure to product concentration and pipeline execution risks warrants monitoring. The lack of disclosed shareholder return data is a minor gap, but not material to the current assessment.

credit_strengths.text: Biogen的槓桿極低，經扣除現金及短期投資後的淨債務對EBITDA比率低於一倍，遠低於行業中位數，反映其資產負債表以保守方式融資。過去三年，公司的債務負擔保持穩定，而現金產生足以覆蓋債務責任。
營運現金流輕鬆覆蓋資本開支，產生的自由現金流佔債務相當大的比例。此現金產生能力，加上流動比率高於兩倍半，提供了強大的流動性緩衝，並支持公司無壓力地履行短期債務的能力。

key_risks.text: 債務到期結構嚴重偏向後期，未來四年內並無到期債務，而第五年則有顯著的集中到期。雖然這降低了短期再融資風險，但公司將需要解決此集中問題，可能需要在不太有利的市場條件下進行再融資。
收入集中於少數已上市產品，以及依賴合作獲取關鍵管道資產（如LEQEMBI和ZURZUVAE），使公司面臨競爭及監管風險。此外，債務票據披露了控制權變更條款，可能要求以溢價回購，增加了事件風險。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率仍然強勁，營運收入覆蓋利息支出多倍。此強勁覆蓋率，加上龐大的現金餘額，提供了充足的能力償還債務，即使營運收入從當前水平大幅下降亦然。
自由現金流對債務比率穩健，且公司的現金流產生一直保持一致。然而，缺乏披露的股息及回購數據限制了對股東分派的可見度，若積極進行，可能吸收現金流並降低債務償還靈活性。

overall_credit_view.text: Biogen呈現強勁的信用狀況，其特點是槓桿極低、利息覆蓋率強勁及流動性充裕。公司的營運表現一直穩定，其債務結構可控，且無短期到期債務。指示性財務風險狀況為極低，且公司相對於行業同業處於有利位置。
展望未來，信用觀點得到預期持續現金產生及可控債務到期結構的支持。然而，公司面臨的產品集中及管道執行風險值得監控。缺乏披露的股東回報數據是一個小缺口，但對當前評估並不重大。
